evidence.claim: Gulf Drive runs north from Longboat Pass onto Anna Maria Island, where the beach lies immediately west of the road in Bradenton Beach.
evidence.quote: SR 789 enters Bradenton Beach and heads into areas of resort homes and businesses, with the beach along the Gulf of Mexico immediately to the west of the road.

evidence.claim: Florida Scenic Highways describes a landscaped waterfront corridor for walking and biking, with beaches, picnic areas and boat ramps along the way.
evidence.quote: The outstanding beaches, picnic areas, boat ramps, parking and scenic vistas along the highway

evidence.claim: Its designation covers Gulf Drive through the city, from the Longboat Pass Bridge to the northern city limits.
evidence.quote: The corridor begins at the Longboat Pass Bridge and extends northward through the City of Bradenton Beach to the northern city limits.

evidence.claim: Gulf Drive runs north from Longboat Pass onto Anna Maria Island
evidence.quote: the road turns to the north and comes to a drawbridge over Longboat Pass. At this point, the state road heads onto Anna Maria Island and becomes Gulf Drive South

evidence.claim: The connection across Longboat Pass first opened in 1926, but the wooden bridge was damaged that year and swept away in 1932.
evidence.quote: the bridge was finished in August. However, the bridge was only open until October, when a hurricane damaged it. On March 6, 1932, the bridge was swept away during a high tide.

evidence.claim: A replacement restored the link to Longboat Key in 1957.
evidence.quote: The connection between Longboat Key and Anna Maria Island was restored in 1957 upon the completion of the current Longboat Pass Bridge.

evidence.claim: That same year, a concrete bridge replaced the wooden crossing from Cortez on the mainland, giving Bradenton Beach another renewed road connection.
evidence.quote: The main wooden bridge to the island from Cortez was replaced by a concrete one in 1957

evidence.claim: An elephant led the parade when Bradenton Beach demonstrated the strength of its new concrete bridge from Cortez in 1957.

evidence.claim: The crossing replaced a wooden bridge, answering residents’ wish for a stronger link to the mainland.

evidence.claim: It remained a toll bridge until 1964 to help recover its cost.

evidence.claim: The town’s name also reflects its mainland ties: during the 1920s land boom, developers used Bradenton Beach instead of Cortez Beach to suggest greater proximity to Bradenton.
evidence.quote: The name "Bradenton Beach" began being used during the mid 1920s as the Florida land boom was occurring. Real estate developers saw this as a way to convince possible buyers that it was closer to Bradenton.

evidence.claim: The Regina carried molasses when it sank on a sandbar off Bradenton Beach on March 8, 1940.
evidence.quote: The Regina, a tanker barge with over 350,000 gallons of molasses onboard and eight crew, sank 200 yards offshore on a sandbar on March 8, 1940.

evidence.claim: Built in Belfast in 1904, the tanker was under tow by Minima when the towline broke near Egmont Key.
evidence.quote: SS Regina was a tanker built in Belfast in 1904

evidence.claim: Both vessels had been trying to reach shelter in Tampa Bay.
evidence.quote: Both vessels had decided to try and go into Tampa Bay seeking shelter because of the weather conditions.

evidence.claim: The cook died while attempting to leave the vessel; the other seven crew members were rescued.
evidence.quote: One of the crew members, its cook and a German Shepherd onboard the ship would die during an attempt to leave the ship. All seven other crew members were rescued.

evidence.claim: In April 2005, the wreck became Florida’s tenth Underwater Archaeological Preserve.
evidence.quote: In April 2005, the wreck became the tenth Florida Underwater Archaeological Preserve.

evidence.claim: the tanker was under tow by Minima when the towline broke near Egmont Key.
